newsitem.title: USA: Toshiba, Varta, Gillette alliance to close plant.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba, Varta, Gillette alliance to close plant.

text.p: 3C Alliance LLP said Tuesday it will stop manufacturing nickel-metal hydride (NiMH) cells at its Mebane facility by September and close the facility by year-end.

The partnership, owned by subsidiaries of Toshiba Corp, Varta AG and Gillette Co's Duracell Inc, manufactures NiMH cells for rechargeable batteries used in portable computers, cellular phones and camcorders.
As a result of this decision, 3C Alliance also said, the partnership will be dissolved.
It said the partner companies intend to cooperate on future development efforts of NiMH technology and will continue to grow market share in the rechargeable battery market.

It said the closing will result in the loss of 152 jobs. The alliance said the decision to close the Mebane facility is part of an evaluation to improve the partners' competitive position as marketers of NiMH cells.

The intense competition of the different battery chemical systems in the rechargeable battery market has resulted in slower growth projections for NiMH cells than previously estimated, it explained. As a result, production will be concentrated in Toshiba Battery's Takasaki, Japan, large scale manufacturing facility to realize cost efficiencies.

"The slower than anticipated growth projections for NiMH cells have adversely affected our cost position and the partners' competitiveness in the rechargeable battery market," stated Bob Correll, 3C Alliance general manager.
"Our evaluation made it clear that closing the facility and concentrating production would yield the cost efficiencies needed to improve that position."
